title: Very comprehensive and easy to use; installation instructions were useless
text: Over the years I have used many different antivirus and internet security products including AVG, Panda, Trend Micro, Symantec (Norton), Bitdefender, McAfee, Webroot, Avast!, Vipre (GFI) and various others.  They all had strengths and weaknesses and eventually I would have to abandon one and move on to another.  I finally settled on one that I have used for a number of years now.  Unfortunately that product had slipped in the ratings in recent years and my subscription was about to run out so decided to try Kaspersky, which I had read very good things about.  Keep in mind that these days a simple anti-virus program isn't enough to keep you secure.  You either need to use multiple products that protect from different kinds of threats or you need a more comprehensive package of protection.  The best security products also now include checking for updates on common programs that most computers have (such as browsers).  Kaspersky Total Security has that.  They also have built in secure browser capability, so you can do online banking without worrying about data being exposed (called Safe Money) and another one called secure connection.  It wasn't clear what the difference between the two is and secure connection is limited to 200mb a day unless you pay extra to remove the limitation.  There is a lot in the product including the ability to encrypt files, a password manager and a system vulnerability scanner and fixer.  It even includes a backup and restore program and parental controls.  It doesn't seem too resource hungry, which is why I had to abandon some products in the past; they just slowed the computer too much.  Overall, it seems like a really nice package and rates highly in virus detection.  You won't go wrong buying this product.  So why only 4 stars?  Well, I am rating the specific package that I got.  I was disappointed when I opened the package, because it is nothing except an activation key and a few pages of instructions.  I ran into problems right away with the instructions.  It recommends signing up at my.kaspersky.com where you can enter and manage your license(s).  I tried repeatedly to add my license after signing up and could not do it; kept getting the message that it wasn't able to and to try again later.  Finally it just said the license had expired.  I gave up and used a different tactic and I recommend you do this too if you buy one of these license packages.  I just went to the main website, downloaded and installed the product.  Then when I ran it, it requested the activation key, which I entered.  Everything went fine then.  A word about support.  When I ran into the difficultly on my.kaspersky.com, I contacted support and they responded very quickly in just a few hours.  I hope this is an indication of their usual levels of support.  I was impressed.  You won't go wrong with Kaspersky, but remember nothing will protect you completely.  There is no substitute for practicing safe computing.  Update: Kaspersky will not install on Windows XP if your disks are FAT32.  Your disks have to be NTFS.  You can convert from FAT32 to NTFS, but there are risks of losing your data if you do that.

title: VERY COMPLEX, RICH PROGRAM WITH BIG LEARNING CURVE
text:
I have used simple drawing programs before, but thought it was time to really try a full featured one. The install of this program went perfectly; no issues at all and was easy; just a few simple questions to answer. It does take a while to install; about 1/2 hour or so on my older PC. The program loads quickly and runs well, even though it is a big program consisting of 5 separate components. It seems comprehensive enough to do any and all graphics work that you might want to accomplish. I was able to create some simple objects and fill them with various colors and text fairly quickly. The programs include some basic tutorials that help you get started, but they aren't extensive enough to really learn the product comprehensively. The box shows some gorgeous drawings that were created with the program. The problem is that you won't be able to quickly create anything that is even close to as good in just a short time. This program takes a real learning commitment. Some things are intuitive, but not everything. If you haven't used a somewhat sophisticated drawing program previously, it will take some time to get up to speed with this. I felt a bit overwhelmed. It's not that there is anything difficult that I encountered; just so much to learn before you can do that much. Some of the terminology had me confused and the number of toolbars and items on them is overwhelming at first. There are tool and menu bars across the top of the screen and toolbars down both sides too. The bars change too, depending on what you are doing. The sheer number of different controls and buttons requires a big time commitment to learn this complex program. It probably also helps to have some drawing skill, especially with a mouse. After working with the main drawing program for a while, I got the feeling that to master this would require a training course. Teaching yourself to use this in the way you want would take far longer than learning it in a class. I didn't spend time looking to see if there were other tutorials or training courses available. I only knocked off one star in my review for the difficulty in learning the product in order to use in an effective way. The product includes access to a lot of on-line art, which is a plus, although I noticed some of that art had watermarks, which would render it less usable and might require an additional subscription fee to remove the watermarks. There is plenty of art that doesn't have the watermarks and you can always capture images or use your own photos as well. If you want a complete, comprehensive drawing program, this is it. Just be prepared to spend a lot of hours learning. I tested on Windows 7, but I'm sure it works fine on 8 and 10 as well.
It has both 32 and 64 bit versions on the disk.

title: Reasonably Good Security Product
text: In the past I used Webroot products, but finally abandoned them as they just took too many resources and slowed my system.  This newer version appears to have been trimmed down a lot, so it should run fast enough on most systems.  My system is rather old, so not as responsive as newer systems with better processors and more memory.  The first scan of my system took under 2 hours, which is about the same as most other products that I have used.  My main criticism of the scanner is that it comes up with a lot of mostly harmless cookies.  That's nice if you really want to clean your system well, but can be misleading in making you think that this product is catching so much more than others, since other scanners often ignore most cookies.  I seem to recall a lot more features in older versions of this software; this version appears to be stripped down somewhat.  That's probably a good thing, as you don't want your security software too complicated or difficult to set up.  It is better if it sits quietly doing it's thing without needing a lot of tweaks.  This seems like an adequate security program for most needs, but apparently lacks a firewall.  I am not overly impressed with it, but it still holds it's own reasonably well against competitors.  I just think there are somewhat better security programs available.

title: Unparalled Protection
text: I have used Panda Antivirus for many years and I can't recall ever getting a virus or at least none that caused any damage.  Once in a while I will check my system with another scanner just to see if Panda is preventing viruses and it appears to be doing an excellent job.  Rarely do I ever find any viruses that are able to slip by Panda.  You won't find a better antivirus prevention program.  It also does a good job on automatic updates.  It's non-intrusive and runs quietly in the background.  The additional protection of the firewall is a plus and the firewall seems to work well too.  Generally I don't like bundled packages, but this combination seems to work flawlessly.  The firewall doesn't have much configurability, so if that's important to you, you might want to just get the antivirus product instead of the combo, but you can turn off the firewall if you want.  The real downside to Panda is that sometimes the install can be a nightmare.  I don't recall having much of an issue with the 2007 version, but some earlier versions were just horrendous.  If you can deal with a sometimes quirky install and finally get it working, the payoff is well worth the struggle.  Some of the easier to install, better known competitors just don't provide as much protection.  Something else to be aware of is that Webroot SpySweeper (a popular anti-spyware program) had some serious conflicts with Panda's scan.  This is not the fault of Panda and Webroot has corrected most of the conflicts in their current version.  There still appears to be one big conflict, but there is a workaround for it.  Panda's support can be a little spotty at times.  Sometimes I have gotten good response; other times it has been a bit slow.  They always seem to respond even if it takes a while.  Since the product works so well once up and running it is rare that you would even need support; most likely you'll need it an install time.  If you are building a new system, install it early and you shouldn't have any issues.  As security products tend to get more comprehensive, there are a bound to be more conflicts and if you try to run multiple products you can have difficulty.  Panda seems no worse (and no better) than any others in that regard.  I highly recommend it even with the caveats mentioned here.

title: Worked well for me, but follow instructions carefully
text:
I wanted to install XP without losing Windows 2000, so I followed the instructions with Partition Magic very carefully and everything worked extremely well. There were a couple of minor glitches, but overall things went much better than I expected. This is a good product, but it is not for the novice. You need to understand the types of partitions and all the issues involved. There is an antimated tutorial that comes with the product and it is very well done and explains some of what you need to know before you proceed. You also MUST create the recovery disks that are recommended. At one point, without the diskettes, I would have been unable to get to one of my partitions and would have had a difficult time getting that partition back. Also backup is recommended, as is checking your disk for errors. If you don't follow the instructions very carefully and understand what you are doing, I can easily see where you could end up with a big mess on your hands. You may need to know how to change your BIOS settings too, in order to boot from a CD, if the OS you are trying to install is on a CD. While a novice might get through it all, this tool is definately better used by those who understand how to install operating systems and how disks are structured and partitioned. I suspect that some exotic configurations with odd disks or operating systems could easily be trashed by this product. It's very powerful and I am extremely pleased that it did what it claimed to be able to do, on my system. Again, if you decide to buy this, it is very important that you read the documentation, view the tutorial and understand what the product is doing and what you are doing. One downside that I encountered is that my USB2 drive is apparently not supported, as PM shows it as BAD, even though the documentation says it supports USB2. Don't buy it with expectations that it will work on a USB drive. I have to say that Symantec has a way of dumbing-down some of their products to the point that they aren't as good anymore as when they were owned by other companies. Although I don't have experience with prior versions of Partition Magic, I do have experience with a couple other products that they bought from other companies. Their versions just don't measure up to the originals. Symantec often gets beat up for poor products, but I think it is partly because thier products are in such wide use.

You can't cover every quirky system out there and the more widely your product is used, the more potential problems. For me, it is a love/hate relationship; I can't live with them and I can't live without them.

title: Not what you want if you have to file a state income tax return
text:
Turbo Tax Basic is at the low end of the line of Turbo Tax CD/download products, both in terms of price and features. Turbo Tax Basic walks you through your tax return, providing step by step guidance. Like other Turbo Tax products, it is reliable and relatively easy to use tax software. My family has been using Turbo Tax software for over 10 years, and we have been pleased with the results.

This basic version of Turbo Tax includes five Federal e-files. It does not include any state income tax software. It does provide you with the option to download the software for your state at a significant extra cost. Considering that over 80 per cent of the states in our country have a state income tax, most users are not going to be satisfied with Turbo Tax Basic. If you invest in Turbo Tax Basic and then decide you need the additional cost state download, you will end up paying more than if you had just shopped around for a good deal on the Turbo Tax Deluxe Federal and State Version in the first place.

If your tax income tax situation does not involve anything complicated, and you're lucky enough to live in Texas or Florida or one of the handful of other states that have no income tax, you may be able to get by with the Turbo Tax Basic version. However, for most people, it is not the way to go--get the Turbo Tax Deluxe version that includes one State download.

title: Brings Anne Frank's world to life!
text:
Anne Frank House: House With A Story is a marvelous tool that enables students a deeper exploration of Anne Frank's world. This is perfect for classroom use in conjunction with studying Anne's diary. You have the chance to explore Prinsengracht from the ground up, searching for hidden memories in the warehouse, offices, and the Franks' hiding quarters. There are numerous small details that truly bring Anne's world to life in a way that the film version never did for me. A narrator reads portions of Anne's diary as that particular section of the house is explored.

Anne's whole world is laid out in astonishing detail, from deeper explorations of her fellow residents-in-hiding, interviews, and short stories. Also included are detailed timelines of a typical day in the Secret Annex, People, and Hidden Places. The CD-ROM features more than 1,000 historical photos, 15 video files (including the only moving pictures of Anne Frank), over 300 slideshows, and four hours of spoken text and other audio effects.

title: "The Little Prince" finally came to life for me
text:
I had read "Le Petit Prince" many years ago when I was a child. It was given to me as a gift, and at the time I put it away. A few years later I dusted it off and gave it another try. Then, in a literature class we read the book again. Many of my friends loved "Le Petit Prince." Our campus in Québec even had a showcase window with all of the "Little Prince" merchandise you could want. But somehow the story was lost on me.
Along came this marvellous software from German publisher Tivola. Contrary to what some reviewers have said, I found that installing and using the software to be very easy. Once I opened the box there was a small manual that covered the interface, gameplay and troubleshooting that got me started on my way.
The game interface on "The Little Prince" is the coolest interactive menu I have ever seen. You start out floating through the universe, past stars, the moon, spinning planets populated by characters from the book...you can move in any direction, accompanied by soothing spacemusic.
There are several different options with the software. You can have the story narrated and click on interactive illustrations, care for the Little Prince's home and rose on Asteroid B-612, explore an interactive biography of the author Antoine de Saint-Éxupéry, play the Fox Taming game on Earth that, when you tame him, you are given access to personalized stationary and a diary. All of the animations and music are top-notch. This is a labour of love that finally breathed life into "Le Petit Prince" for me. I entered his world and saw things through his eyes. Perfect for children of all ages (including grown-up ones).

title: Great for those looking for an introduction to languages
text:
A few years ago I bought 31 Languages of the World by Transparent Software and I was impressed by the number of languages, games and activities. When I saw that they had released 101 Languages of the world I couldn't resist!
As someone who works with 4+ languages on a daily basis, I also enjoy studying languages as a hobby. It was fascinating to see some of the lesser studied European languages and variants such as Asturian, Provençal, Basque, and Catalan.
The games provided are great for reviewing or brushing up on vocabulary and grammar. Recording conversations and completing dialogues was also very helpful to get a feel for phrasing and pronunciation.
It is refreshing to see a software company taking the effort to enlist native speakers and record unusual languages, such as Blackfoot, Quechua, Hawaiian, Welsh, Xhosa, Wolof, and even some that I was not familiar with.
The important thing to remember is that no, using this product will not make you fluent. It will introduce you to grammar, pronunciation, culture, and common phrases. Native speakers are a plus, but I did not like the fact that languages that made use of symbols rather than letters were Romanized, such as Japanese, Chinese, Arabic, etc. In the long run it is much more difficult to pick up the symbols after learning the language.
Still, this is a great product at a reasonable price for anyone with an interest in languages, either learning for the first time or for reviewing. Give this software a try, have fun, and good luck!

title: Decent, But Expensive; Not Fully Functional on New Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Tablet
text:
CROSSWORDS by Standalone is a decent crossword puzzle app, but inflexible and expensive. On my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" tablet, the working display shows about two-thirds of a weekday NY Times puzzle grid, and I can't find any way to resize the grid to show the whole puzzle at once. (You must swipe down or hit an arrow button to reveal the lower one-third of the grid.) The Across and Down clues appear alongside the grid in a readable typeface, but the clues are cut off at the right. (Perhaps this is an 8.9" Kindle Fire HD issue that the developer will correct; fortunately, clicking on a cut-off clue will display the full clue below the grid.)

The puzzle hints--found under the list icon beside the app icon, at the left--don't always work as expected. For example, "reveal entire puzzle" only filled in one word (for the 1-down clue) when I started from the "hints for 1-down" screen. In contrast, "reveal entire puzzle" filled in the entire puzzle when I started from a "press-and-hold-on-clue" popup. Worse, the general settings for navigation (e.g., "skip filled squares", "show mistakes") don't seem to function at all. (Perhaps this is another Kindle Fire HD issue for the developer to fix.)

The app allows you to enter multiple letters in a single square, and to look up puzzle info (must-haves for NY Times crossword solvers). If you are a NY Times crosswords subscriber, the app will automatically download the daily puzzles for you. The app comes with an assortment of puzzles already installed, and allows you to browse for and download many more puzzles from the Internet. It also allows you to establish an account and compare your times with other solvers.

However, the FREE [[ASIN:B005U6QIMI Crosswords Plus]] app does nearly all of the same things. (Crosswords Plus does not download your NY Times subscription puzzles automatically, although it makes it easy to download them daily; it doesn't come with puzzles loaded, although it points you to free Internet sources; and it doesn't have a feature for comparing scores with other solvers.) In addition, [[ASIN:B005U6QIMI Crosswords Plus]] allows you to resize the grid, offers an alternate clues-only view, includes the usual hints options, and has navigational settings (skipping boxes, etc.) that are fully functional on the Kindle Fire HD 8.9" tablet.

Even if this CROSSWORDS app worked perfectly, I would still prefer [[ASIN:B005U6QIMI Crosswords Plus]]. For this reason, and because of the high price and current Kindle Fire HD 8.9" tablet issues, I rate CROSSWORDS at 3 stars.

title: App Purchased for 1st Gen Fire Works With New Fire HD 8.9" Tablet
text:
Right after the 1st Gen Kindle Fire was released, I started using the original GSam Battery Monitor (then known as the Badass Battery Monitor) as a one-tap solution to monitoring the Fire's remaining charge and battery usage. I liked the app so well, I upgraded to the special Kindle Fire version when it was released, and have been using it ever since.

Today I received my Kindle Fire HD 8.9" Wi-Fi tablet, and was delighted to find that this GSam Battery Monitor (Kindle Tablet Edition) works with new tablet as well! There was no need to purchase another version that was specifically designed for the larger tablet--which was NOT the case with many of my existing 1st Gen Kindle Fire apps. You only need to download your purchased app and install it. You can then check your battery usage and charge by swiping down from the top of the 8.9" screen.

Kudos to the GSam developer, for issuing regular updates and improvements to the original, excellent battery app, and for having it immediately ready to go with the new, larger Kindle Fire tablets.

title: Nice Concept, Decimal Point Hard to Find on Kindle Fire
text:
The concept is nice, but the decimal point is hard to find on the Kindle Fire (software v. 6.03). When I open the app or one of its calculator options (Percent, Percent Increase, Percent Discount, Tip Calculator, Percent Margin, Percentage Change, Percentage of), only the keyboard shows--and the keyboard has NO decimal point/period key.

If I turn the Kindle Fire to change the display from horizontal to vertical, or vice versa, the "spell checker" line with punctuation options USUALLY appears above the keyboard. This line includes a decimal point/period that works for purposes of entering the calculations. Also, if I hit the "x" inside the number entry box (the "x" is in gray, at the right), it will USUALLY bring up the punctuation options line. Hitting the "x" in the number entry box also clears the numbers in the box.

I rather like the Tip Calculator, which makes it easy to divide a restaurant check for a group of people. When you input the check total, the number of people, and the tip percentage, the app will return each person's share (including her/his share of the tip).

However, this app is awkward to use, if you have to work to get a decimal point option for entering decimal or dollar and cent amounts. If the developer should update the app to fix this Kindle Fire flaw, I would rate the app at 4 or 5 stars.

title: Monitors Kindle Fire's Battery Charge, Estimates Time Left, Analyzes Individual App Usage
text:
Excellent one-tap solution to monitoring the Kindle Fire's remaining charge and battery usage. This app tells you how the battery is actually being used (percentages for screen, wi-fi active, held awake, app usage); and sends notifications (to the notification area at the top left of the home screen) that include the current charge level plus an estimate of the time left (based on your average usage).

If you choose "App Sucker" from the list menu, you see a list of apps that shows the percentage of battery consumed by each app. If you select a particular app, you get detailed stats on CPU usage, keep awake, wake locks, bytes sent and received, included packages, included processes, etc. These stats let you know which apps are power-hungry, and what they're doing.

This is exactly what I wanted for my Kindle Fire. Another battery monitor, [[ASIN:B004T555WA BatteryTime Lite]], which is apparently designed for cell phones, didn't work for me because it requires entry of the Kindle Fire's battery capacity (a figure that I don't have). This [[ASIN:B00658U5HE Badass Battery Monitor]] works off the Kindle Fire's battery charge level, so it works "out of the box" without needing any additional technical information.

EDITED 11/16/12:
I liked this app so well, that I purchased the version made specifically for the 1st Gen Kindle Fire (the [[ASIN:B006TH5I28 GSam Battery Monitor (Kindle Tablet Edition)]]). Today I received my wi-fi Kindle Fire HD 8.9" tablet, and was delighted to find that the GSam Battery Monitor app for the Fire works with the new tablet, too. I didn't have to purchase a new version, as I did with quite a few of my existing non-HD Fire apps.

Purchase of a product key card for Microsoft Office 2010 saved me a substantial amount of money, given that I needed only one license. (The CDROM product provides licenses for installation on two computers, e.g., a purchaser's desktop and laptop.)

Office 2010 was not preloaded on my target computer, so I downloaded the software from the web site named in the key card instructions. The web site gives you the option of purchasing a backup CDROM if you're a nervous nellie like me. The web site also gives clear instructions on how to proceed after the download.

The software download (585MB) took about two hours with a relatively slow DSL connection. Installing the software requires the product key to be entered for a second time (include the hyphens). The installation itself took about 15 minutes on a 1.67 GHz netbook, which had a trial version of Microsoft Office 2007 installed that needed to be removed. (The installation screen gave the option of removing a previous Office installation or leaving all or parts of a previous installation on the computer.)

As often happens with Microsoft products, the "installation progress bar" finished a few minutes before the installation itself was finished. The product then required a reboot to finalize the installation. For me, the only really anxious moments involved in the entire operation were the moments spent waiting and watching the screen while the computer was verifying the legitimacy of the product key.

title: Installation for me was horrendous but I was able to crop one video
text:
I have a Dell Inspiron 1720 with Windows Vista SP2 installed, 3GB of RAM and more disk space than I need. My processor is an Intel Pentium T2310 / 1.46 GHz which is a touch less than recommended.

I chose the full install. During setup, the CD just churns, and churns, and churns, and churns. After 70 minutes of churning, I used the Task Manager to abort the install because the setup got stuck on installing FastFlick.

I then tried to re-install again but chose a custom install and removed FastFlick. When I did that I got a message partway into the install that said, "Setup encountered an error during installation. Error Code: 0652." I then looked on their forum site for an answer but there was just a post by someone else who got the error but didn't receive any feedback on it. (That's not very good support.)

I aborted this install, went into the Control Panel, and uninstalled everything it had installed before (which I had to do one by one in a long drawn-out process). I then rebooted and tried the custom install again being sure to remove FastFlick. Once I did that about 1 hour later the product finished installing without that component.

Next I tried to use the software. Since this was the first time, I kept getting a registration screen. After I filled out my name and email for registration, I got this error message "Our servers are not responding. We apologize for the inconvenience; please try again at a later time." Luckily after it goes through the motions, I'm able to bypass the error and use the product. However, since the product never got registered, I get the registration screen repeatedly every time I load Roxio which is very annoying.

After some fiddling around using their advanced video editing, I figured out how to crop a video and save a portion of it to a file that can be played with Windows Media Player. There is a learning center section of the software but no real user guide in the format I was looking for; only lots of tips.

Besides cropping the video, I also tried to burn my 229.2Mb project to a Memorex CD-RW Platinum that had 654MB capacity. These disks were brand new. The first one I tried it said it had zero Mb available. The next disk I tried said the correct capacity 656.1 MB but then said I couldn't burn to that disk and kept spitting it out and asking me to insert valid media. I was disappointed with the inconsistency of the Mb reported between the two disks even though I finaly realized that I probably needed a DVD Read/Write disk. I then tried just burning the video file to disk. Although this worked, it was a file that could not be played because it had the DMSD extension. I then looked for the MPG file I created previously and burned that to disk. This worked and I was able to play back the file on another laptop as long as I used Window Explorer to find the file on CD with Windows Media Player installed to play it.

In summary, I spent almost 3-1/2 hours trying to install this product and ended up with a partial install of what was available to install (remember FastFlick would not install). I then spent another 1-1/2 hours trying to figure out the software, cropping my video and burning the production to a CD ROM disk. Also, the product license only allows an installation on one machine. Obviously I've only scratched the surface with what this product claims it can do. I'm also totally new to this type of software, so there's a steep learning curve on my part. No user manual is supplied in the Learning Center (at least none I could find) and all I found in the Roxio knowledge base online was a user manual for a very old version of the product (Creator 2010). I do very much like that I was able to crop a 2-minute piece of video from a 2 hour production and then burn the file to DVD and it did a very good job of that so I'm satisfied in that regard. However, getting that far was such a hassle than I can only rate this product 2 stars until all the kinks such as support and install issues are worked out.

So far so good, and i decided that i needed to see if my tempo and count were correct, I decided to add this program to my learning tools. I have to say, this is a great program to see how much you have progressed on your own. I found the exercises helped to reinforce the beat, the sight reading of the left hand and music theory. Actually, I really recommend you learn from the text book and then come to this program, as you will get a lot more out of it than just using this program on its own:it does go a little fast.

The program offers music theory, sight reading, ear training tests, lots of little tests to see how much you have learnt thus far, video to explain the positioning of the hand, audio explanations; the finger tracker, which is the best part of the program as it tells at the end, the percentage accuracy of your playing. And if you get frustrated at not getting above 95%, for the perfectionist, you can hit a key that plays it back to you on how it should be played! Note that if you hit a wrong note that also counts against you as well as not hitting it or holding it for the right amount of time! You can go back to a previous lesson again and again, which helps to reinforce the point. There are so many little helpers on each lesson, like video or audio pointers.

There are over 300 lessons, so I am looking forward to plowing through them along with the Alfred's course, which compliments this program beautifully. You will need to have a MIDI cable to connect the computer/laptop to your digital piano, which Amazon also sells at a very good price. So worth the money in lieu of a teacher. title: A Good Alternative or Supplement to Duolingo or Rosetta Stone
text:
I have been trying to learn Spanish with a couple high school years from 30 some years ago, Duolingo, and by reading a number of Spanish language books like Harry Potter, The Lion The Witch and the wardrobe. When I got a chance to get a reviewer subscription to Babbel.com I jumped at it.

Initially, I kind of didn't like Babbel. It seemed a little clumsy. You need to do a lot of typing, which doesn't work well on my iPhone and was somewhat frustrating on my ipad as the window jumped around when the keyboard came up. But when I pulled it up on my touch screen laptop, it really worked fairly well. And, once I got over the "inconvenience" of having to type in Spanish words (something Duolingo seems to have limited,) I found that it really helped me to focus on gender and spellings. It actually became a very good teaching tool, although it took a little familiarity. You are prompted with lettered buttons that show the letters in the word, which seems like a little too much for a cue.

I really liked a number of things that helped my learning. First, it features a different word set than duolingo, even for the same objects. I like that I got a different vocabulary. I also liked that they would put the beginner words into sentences that were unapologetically complex. It was nice to have more challenging sentences than could be made with the beginner words and when I sampled intermediate and advanced levels, I found that Advanced is an immersion experience that I really like. Lastly, I think that Babbel does a better job of giving helpful rules for Spanish. They are brief but seem to stick.

The bad things I found was that it gets a little repetitive and grows a little tiring. One of the beginner features is speech recognition which is not working well for me. Duolingo speech recognition seems a little more tolerant. With Babbel I find there are some words and phrases it will just not recognize, but this actually focuses me on pronunciation, so this might be good, if a little frustrating. Definitely use a headset as built in microphones definitely don't work as well.

All in all, a good resource with its pros and cons. It might be in line with duolingo which has the advantage of being free. But this is a fantastic supplement to Duolingo, and a combination and going back and forth might keep things fresh.

I batched a series of images of Marmots and Ground Squirrels in Alaska and took them from worthless to perfect in no time (if you subtract the time it took me to figure out how to get them all batch selected and then converted.

Also, I have used the Photoshop plug in and this built in option is more like the plug in and less dynamic than Photomatix. Or at least with my current abilities. I can get it to make decent HDR images again testing with Alaskan images of glaciers, but I cannot get that unworldly look. Not sure if that is me, or not in the abilities of this software. But I was able to get highlights on the ice as well as details in underbrush so that is success.

Other things - It does look like there is a learning curve and I am still early in the process. I have many photos from over the years and hope to shoot some to start populating catalogs and seeing how this affects my work flow. I'm looking forward to trying more batch corrections and occasional clean up with the editing tools. title: A Fantastic Overview of Dream Weaver and Web Design in General
text:
I've been creating websites with Dreamweaver for years now, and all that experience has taught me one thing - I'm a hack web designer. Recently I have been trying to learn industry CSS standards and had heard that Dreamweaver has made great advances in CSS management in CS4 and CS5. I'm embarrassed to say what version I am using.

When I got a chance to get a reviewer copy of this training set I jumped for two reasons, first I was mulling over spending the money to upgrade to DW CS5 and I second I have always that I was missing out on a lot of DW's capabilities. It's now obvious that I should upgrade for the CSS management upgrades alone.

As for the value of the training - I couldn't be happier. This is not an advanced tips and tricks resource, nor is it an exhaustive boot camp in web page authoring, but it is a fairly thorough training taking you from site planning and design to creation and publishing. I watched the videos from beginning to end and they start pretty basic with an HTML refresher then move to the meatier DW specific training. I can see myself returning to several sections later to brush up.

Personally, the CSS, Media, and Forms training videos were enough to justify the price tag. The training lessons were short and easily digestible. I liked that it broke training into 3-10 minutes so I had some time to do a little more in-depth googling on subjects like text wrapping on absolute positioned CSS objects (which it won't.) or checking my version of DW.

What this is
- An Adobe Certification Training Aid - so it starts from a very low level introduction and goes through the entire DW web creation process
- A wonderfully designed interface
- A great overview of using DW

What it isn't
- A substitute for spending the time working with DW (but it will jump start a novice)
- An expert tips and tricks reference

All in all, I highly recommend this to anyone trying to learn DW or even web design in general. The CSS placement section has been the most enlightening coverage of the topic I have been able to find. The author's delivery on the videos is great and the interface is the best, most intuitive I have seen. The only bad thing I can say is that the closed captioning is defaulted on, so at times it covered the bottom of the properties table at the bottom of the screen. So sometimes I had to close it to see things the author was pointing out. But all in all, this is an absolutely wonderful product.

title: Gold Standard!!
text:
Rosetta Stone is the gold standard for a reason. You learn a language in the same way you learned your native tongue, not by memorization. This package gives you acess to an app that can be accessed from any device. Please note that you can only be logged in to one device at a time. The mobile app allows you to download lessons to study offline. I will give some info about the Mandarin course just in case there are others who want this information.

The Mandarin course is split into 20 units. Each unit (usually) has four core lessons that have the following elements: core lesson, pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, reading, and writing. Each lesson takes about 45 minutes at a standard pace. The tone you use in Mandarin is very important and can change the meaning of a word. The four basic tones (and the neutral tone) aren't explicitly taught in these lessons, but you can go to YouTube to learn them in less than 10 minutes. The app uses your mic function to allow you to practice pronunciation. You can choose to do the lessons with simplified Chinese characters, Pinyin (alphabet characters known as hàn) or both. I suggest the first option if you want to be able to read in Chinese. The default is Pinyin, but you can change that by toggling between the icons at the bottom of the lesson progress bar.

If you have access to a streaming service that offers Chinese-language shows, I would recommend watching shows/movies to reinforce your lessons. You'll get used to hearing native speakers and your pronunciation will improve. It's also a great way to pick up vocabulary. I recommend Viki Rakuten. There are lots of programs available including shows that are currently airing.
